english: Let $f:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be a continuous function with $f(0)=0$ and $f(x)>0$ for $x>0$, which is differentiable on $(0,\infty)$. For each $x>0$, let $M$ be the foot of the perpendicular from the point $P(x,f(x))$ to the $x$-axis, and let the normal to the curve $y=f(x)$ at $P$ meet the $x$-axis at $N$. Suppose that $MN=3x\sqrt{x^{2}+9}$ for every $x>0$. Then the value of $f(4)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ एक सतत फलन है जिसके लिए $f(0)=0$ तथा $x>0$ के लिए $f(x)>0$ है, और $f$, $(0,\infty)$ पर अवकलनीय है। प्रत्येक $x>0$ के लिए, माना कि बिन्दु $P(x,f(x))$ से $x$-अक्ष पर डाले गए लम्ब का पाद $M$ है, तथा $P$ पर वक्र $y=f(x)$ का अभिलम्ब $x$-अक्ष को $N$ पर मिलता है। माना कि प्रत्येक $x>0$ के लिए $MN=3x\sqrt{x^{2}+9}$ है। तब $f(4)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Normal at $P(x,y)$ meets the $x$-axis at $N(x+yy',0)$, so $MN=|yy'|$ (the subnormal)
If $yy'<0$ somewhere, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(y^{2})<0$ there; since $|yy'|>0$ for all $x>0$ the sign is constant, and $y^{2}$ cannot decrease from $y(0)^{2}=0$. So $yy'=3x\sqrt{x^{2}+9}$
solution_full: Write $y=f(x)$. The normal at $P(x,y)$ is $X-x+y'(Y-y)=0$. Putting $Y=0$ gives $X=x+yy'$, so $N=(x+yy',0)$ while $M=(x,0)$. Hence $MN=|yy'|$.
The condition is $|yy'|=3x\sqrt{x^{2}+9}$, which is positive for every $x>0$. Since $yy'=\dfrac12\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(y^{2}\right)$ is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ and never zero, it has one sign there.
If it were negative, $y^{2}$ would be strictly decreasing on $(0,\infty)$; but $y^{2}\to0$ as $x\to0^{+}$ and $y^{2}>0$ for $x>0$, which is impossible. So $yy'=3x\sqrt{x^{2}+9}$.
originality_note: New: the curve is defined by the length of its subnormal MN, given as 3x sqrt(x^2+9), with the curve starting at the origin; the sign of yy' must be argued before separating, and the integral needs the substitution u = x^2 + 9 (way 5). Closest known: textbook curves whose subnormal is constant or proportional to x. Different because: the length condition hides a sign decision and the starting point is the origin, where the equation is degenerate.
key_step: Reading MN as the subnormal |yy'|, fixing its sign from f(0)=0, then the substitution u = x^2 + 9.
justification: Three linked stages (geometric translation with a sign argument, separation, substitution) in numerical format. Above 2026-P2-Q3 (L2) because of the geometric set-up and the sign decision; comparable to 2025-P2-Q9 (L2) plus a stage, so L3.

concept_use.Integration by substitution: The integral of 3x sqrt(x^2+9) is found by the substitution u = x^2 + 9, giving (x^2+9)^(3/2).
concept_use.Variable separable equations: The subnormal condition gives y dy/dx = 3x sqrt(x^2+9), whose variables separate to y^2/2 = (x^2+9)^(3/2) + C.
